title: Cast Iron vs. PVC in Modern Drainage Systems
description: Choosing between cast iron and PVC for DWV (Drain, Waste, and Vent) systems involves balancing acoustic performance, fire resistance, and installation efficiency. Cast iron pipe excels at muffling fluid movement noise due to its dense molecular structure, making it ideal for multi-family residential stacks and commercial drop ceilings. Additionally, cast iron is non-combustible and does not emit toxic fumes during a building fire. PVC is lightweight, highly chemical resistant, and significantly faster to join using solvent cement, making it cost-effective for single-family residences. Understanding these material characteristics ensures correct application based on project noise and safety requirements.
